record.context_brief: Normal and conormal skew lattice varieties
record.original_question: Describe the subvariety of skew lattices generated jointly by the variety of normal skew lattices and the variety of conormal skew lattices.

evidence.quote: What can one say about the subvariety of skew lattices generated jointly from the varieties of normal and conormal skew lattices?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A skew lattice is an algebra $(S; \wedge, \vee)$ where $\wedge$ and $\vee$ are associative, idempotent binary operations satisfying the absorption identities $x \wedge (x \vee y) = x = x \vee (x \wedge y)$ and $(x \wedge y) \vee y = y = (x \vee y) \wedge y$. A skew lattice is called normal if it satisfies the identity
$$x \wedge y \wedge z \wedge w = x \wedge z \wedge y \wedge w,$$
and conormal if it satisfies the dual identity
$$x \vee y \vee z \vee w = x \vee z \vee y \vee w.$$
The normal skew lattices form a variety $\mathbf{N}$ and the conormal skew lattices form a variety $\mathbf{C}$, each being a subvariety of the variety $\mathbf{SL}$ of all skew lattices. Let $\mathbf{N} \vee \mathbf{C}$ denote the join of $\mathbf{N}$ and $\mathbf{C}$ in the lattice of subvarieties of $\mathbf{SL}$, i.e., the smallest subvariety of $\mathbf{SL}$ containing both $\mathbf{N}$ and $\mathbf{C}$.

Describe the variety $\mathbf{N} \vee \mathbf{C}$: find a set of identities axiomatizing it (relative to $\mathbf{SL}$), and characterize its members structurally.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as an open question in a 2018 collection of problems on noncommutative structures. A web search did not locate any subsequent publication providing a description or axiomatization of the join of the normal and conormal skew lattice varieties, so the problem appears to remain open.
